No numpy dependency added -- the package's own adapters/ directory already exists empty specifically for "optional NRRD ecosystem adapters", so a numpy layer, if ever built, belongs there as additive work, not a hard dependency; this stays consistent with format-factory-core's and format-factory-ora's own zero-dependency, bounded-reader design. Per-axis metadata (kind, label, unit, spacing, axis min/max, center, thickness, space direction) follows every operation: transpose reorders it; flip swaps axis_min/axis_max, negates space_direction, and shifts space_origin by (size-1)*old_direction to keep the view's own first element pinned at its pre-flip world-space position; slice/crop shift axis_min/axis_max by start*spacing when spacing is known, else clear them (None) rather than carry a stale bound forward -- a disclosed simplification (cell-vs-node centers nuance is not modelled). A "range" kind axis (SAL-NRRD-00022, KIND_REQUIRED_SIZE not None -- e.g. a 3-color channel axis) refuses a slice/crop that would change its own element count, since that would change what the sample means, not resample it.
